observation: Architecture-critique closed in exactly 2 rounds and prevented 2 genuine correctness bugs from reaching build: round 1 found W2 (a second, divergent coalescing signal between the poll path and manual-trigger route that would let two concurrent runs fire for one routine) and W3 (a new 'running run, no session' state the reaper doesn't cover, which a terminal PROVISION failure would leave stuck forever). Both were source-verified against the live worktree, not the plan's prose, and both were fixed for real in round 2 (unified onto findRunningRoutineRun; failOrRelease finalizes via updateRoutineRunIfRunning). Matches compound candidate C5 (architecture-critique fact-audit catches false claims about existing code) — protect this practice.

Round-1 W3 was a generic reviewer flag ('reaper coverage gap for the new running-run-with-no-session state, add a test') but the planner's round-2 revision did the harder-than-asked thing: it enumerated every terminal state and found a MORE SPECIFIC real bug the generic flag hadn't named — a pre-hand-off terminal INTENT failure (routine deactivated between fire and drain) also stuck a routineRun in 'running' with no session, and coalescing would brick that routine permanently. Round-2 critique explicitly credits this ('the planner did the harder-than-asked thing... found the genuine gap my round-1 W3 pointed at only generically'). Worth protecting: a reviewer's generic correctness flag, taken seriously, can surface a bug the reviewer itself only gestured at.

Round-1 W1 flagged that the agent_work_intents full single-owner-guard deferral was prose-only inside plans/AU15/ (which retires at write-docs) — the exact silent-vanish pattern already confirmed twice on this track (Settings/Notification raw-write gap, and AU12 shipping with named carve-outs still open, per project memory feedback/AU-track-status). Round-2 verified the planner registered it durably instead: a substantive, named section inside the TRACKED .pipeline/work-packages/TRACK-AU.md, inside AU8's own section, naming the table, the two owner modules, the sanctioned write helper, and the three non-owner accessors that must migrate first. This is the discipline AU13 credits for becoming a real guard instead of a footnote — worth protecting as the pattern for any WP that must defer scope to a future WP.

Builder deviated from the plan's suggested proof path (repoint packages/eval/src/scenarios/delegation.ts through checkAndFireRoutine+drain) because doing so would require a 4th export on packages/server/src/routines.ts, which AU11's zero-allowlist runtime-ownership-guard locks to exactly 3 exports with an explicit 'do not add exports' warning. Builder refused to loosen another track's locked guard and instead moved the delegate-selection proof into agent-work-intent-worker.routine-selection.integration.test.ts, driving the real drainAgentWorkIntents -> resolveAuthoritativeInput -> selectAgentByAppDefaults path against real seeded owner+delegate data. Code review verified the au11 guard stayed green (no 4th export) and confirmed this is genuine end-to-end proof, not a structural stand-in — ruled the deviation correct and non-under-delivering. Good instance of a builder holding a cross-track locked invariant instead of loosening it for local convenience.

Code review passed DONE on the first round: 0 CRITICAL, 0 blocking WARNING, 3 non-blocking observations. Reviewer independently re-ran npm run check/lint/knip:production and every guard (au6/au9/au11/au13/au14) on the current tree rather than trusting the builder's report, and independently grepped all 5 changed production files for raw routines/routineRuns/agentWorkIntents access to verify the founder read+write ownership directive in the actual diff. Continues the reviewer-independently-reverifies-not-trusts pattern seen in AU10/AU11/AU16.

DoD (dod.md) and the round-1 plan assumed scripts/au6-agent-boundary-guard.ts already had a --fixtures self-test harness (au13-style) to prove the new file-scoped rules positive/negative/scoping cases. It did not — au6 was a plain --check-only regex scan. This was only caught in architecture-critique round 1 (W4), not before, meaning the DoD had to be revised and the builder had to build a whole new self-test harness (au13-style fixture writer + inspect() assertions) during the green phase rather than it being pre-existing infra. Second known instance of a WP's DoD assuming test-harness infra that doesn't exist yet (au13 built its own fixtures harness from scratch too) — worth checking DoD-authoring guidance for 'does the referenced test/guard harness actually exist' as a standing pre-flight check.

Code review's non-blocking observation #1: the new au6 --fixtures self-test is not wired into npm run lint (only --check runs live) — identical to the au13 precedent where the fixtures self-test is a dev-run-only self-test and the live --check is the actual CI gate. Reviewer judged this acceptable since the file-scoped rules ARE enforced live via --check. This is now a 2-occurrence pattern (au13, au6) of guard fixtures harnesses existing but not gate-wired — worth watching as an EMERGING compound candidate if a third guard repeats it.

Cost/cycle summary for AU15: 8 commits (plan+DoD, critique round 1, plan revision, critique round 2, red, green, attestation, code-review), architecture-critique took exactly 2 rounds (round 1 NEEDS REVISION with 4 WARNINGs, 0 CRITICAL; round 2 DONE, all 4 resolved, 0 remaining findings), code review 1 round (DONE, 0 CRITICAL/0 blocking WARNING, 3 non-blocking notes), zero reverts/force-pushes. All 4 pre-build WARNINGs were closed with real mechanism fixes (not reworded acknowledgments) before the builder wrote a line, and the one build-phase scope call was judged correct by review. Clean baseline for a WP whose plan needed real revision but whose build then went smoothly.
